newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican tequila makers see more European exports.
newsitem.headline: Mexican tequila makers see more European exports.

text.p: Mexican tequila makers expect more exports to Europe after getting official recognition linking the name 'tequila' to the liquor's place of origin.
"We currently export 10 percent of output to Europe, but in two to three years we could double that," said Carlos Orendain, president of the Orendain tequila distillers.
"Now there will be genuine tequila in Europe...and we can produce enough to meet demand there."

Word was finally received from Brussels on Thursday that only tequila made in its place of origin, according to Mexican government rules could be sold in the European Union under that name, said a news release from distiller Cuervo.

The agreement came after four years of negotiations and confers on tequila a status similar to wines protected under the French "appellation controlee", where only wines grown in a certain area may have a particular name.
The Cuervo firm, which has been distilling tequila for two centuries, estimated the new agreement would pave the way for an additional 1,440,000 liters to be sold per year.

In Mexico, tequila must be made in wooden vats from the Weber strain of the blue agave plant grown for eight years and made Mexico only authorizes tequila made in four states to be labeled under that name.
Tequila bottled immediately after distilling is labelled "white tequila"; after two months as "stored"; after four months it is "medium-dry"; and after at least one year it is called "aged."
